title: Asymmetric warmup storm caused circuit hysteresis and secondary-region SLO regression
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Postmortem for a multi-region incident where an asymmetric cache warmup pattern during planned maintenance triggered a cascade of circuit-breaker openings and priority-queue shedding, resulting in a ~23% SLO miss for tail latency across EU region customers. This document describes timeline, root cause analysis, mitigation, and concrete follow-ups.
timeline: 2026-02-24T03:12:00Z - Planned maintenance: rolling kernel patch in us-east-1 control plane; traffic routing rules were switched to prefer eu-west-1 for failover testing.
2026-02-24T03:13:40Z - Traffic shift completed; eu-west-1 observed a +3.8x spike in new cold sessions over 5 minutes.
2026-02-24T03:15:22Z - Queue depth for priority pool in eu-west-1 exceeded soft threshold (1200 -> 2100) causing backpressure into controller.
2026-02-24T03:16:10Z - Circuit breakers on heterogeneous model-serving pods started transitioning to OPEN due to sustained 95th/99th token latency increases.
2026-02-24T03:17:00Z - Autoscaling did not respond quickly because warmup cost (KV loads + model cold-start kernels) dominated; secondary-region pods hit CPU/GPU memory pressure.

2026-02-24T03:24:00Z - Partial mitigation: manually increased priority queue capacity and temporarily relaxed circuit hysteresis; tail latency recovered slowly but residual SLO misses persisted until 2026-02-24T04:05:00Z.
2026-02-24T05:00:00Z - Incident declared resolved; postmortem investigation initiated.
2026-02-27T10:00:00Z - Internal review and cross-team retrospective held with Eng, SRE, Product, and Console teams.
impact_summary: Customer-facing 99th percentile token latency SLO (100ms target) breached for 22.9% of affected requests in eu-west-1 during the 03:12-04:05 UTC window. No data loss or incorrect outputs were observed. Several high-throughput tenants saw degraded tail latency and increased retries; console alerts and some automated retry loops amplified traffic to the region.
root_cause: Three interacting factors: (1) asymmetric warmup storm: when failover traffic landed in eu-west-1 it generated a concentrated set of cold KV cache fills and kernel path ramps (attention cache + quantized kernel paths) that increased per-request service time; (2) circuit-breaker hysteresis miscalibration: CB policies used conservative cooldown windows and open thresholds tuned for steady-state fanout but not for large cold warmups, causing circuits to remain open overly long and preventing quick recovery; (3) queue threshold tuning and priority inversion: soft queue thresholds triggered shedding of non-priority traffic but head-of-line cold requests held hot resources, blocking higher-priority live requests and delaying autoscaler-driven pod readiness.
contributing_factors: Runbook failover test routing applied without a staged traffic ramp, console auto-retry loops reissued timed-out requests increasing load, and autoscaler ramp limits (min replicas and scale-rate) were too restrictive for rapid cold-start-dominated spikes.
what_we_did_immediately: Relaxed circuit hysteresis for eu-west-1 (reduced cooldown from 180s -> 45s) to allow faster re-closures.
Increased priority queue soft limit by 2x and enabled temporary admission-control to drop known low-value background workloads.
Manual burst scaling: added 8 warm GPU pods in eu-west-1 and preloaded KV cache for top-20 tenants.
Applied emergency routing rule to distribute new sessions across us-east-2 and eu-west-1 to reduce concentration.
Disabled console automated retry policy for 30 minutes to prevent amplification.
long_term_actions: Adaptive warmup-aware routing: implement staged traffic ramp when shifting regions (owner: Marco Li, estimate: 8).
Circuit-breaker rewrite: add an adaptive hysteresis layer that considers recent warmup indicators and not just error/latency counts (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 5).
Queue admission redesign: introduce head-of-line detection and preferential preemption for cold-warmup work to reduce priority inversion (owner: Lukas Meyer, estimate: 8).
Autoscaler policy changes: allow rapid temporary overprovisioning for cold-start events and add a warm-pod prefetcher that preloads top-model KV state (owner: SRE team, estimate: 5).
Runbook and test updates: add a staged-failover test to CI that simulates cache-cold traffic spikes and validates circuit hysteresis behavior (owner: Reliability Guild, estimate: 3).
Console safeguards: add flagging and throttling of automated retries from tenant control planes; add visibility for amplification risk (owner: Console, estimate: 3).
Model-serving improvements: optimize KV fetch batching during warmup and add fast-path kernel selection to reduce the cold-request service time (owner: Runtime team, estimate: 8).

postmortem_notes: During the retrospective engineering and SRE agreed that similar incidents may recur when traffic is rapidly shifted between regions for maintenance or testing. The key lesson is that cold-start dynamics change the optimal control loop behavior; static thresholds tuned for steady-state throughput are insufficient. We will prioritize features that make control policies warmup-aware and make failovers conservative by default with opt-in aggressive routes for emergency-only scenarios.
status_notes: All action items created and triaged. First prototypes (ENG-864211) scheduled as canary for runtime-1.23 alpha by 2026-03-31. Runbook and CI tests targeted for next week. Priority: follow through on adaptive CB and staged ramp before next cross-region maintenance window.
